units.title: 2b Content of A Level English Literature

outcomes.text: Study at least eight texts, with at least two each of prose, poetry and drama.
Include at least three pre-1900 texts including one Shakespeare play, one text first published or performed after 2000, and one unseen text.
Understand how writers shape meanings in texts.
Understand how different readers, including over time, interpret texts.
Understand how texts relate to one another and to literary traditions, movements and genres.
Understand the significance of cultural and contextual influences on readers and writers.
Study one Shakespeare play from Hamlet, King Lear, Othello, Richard III, The Taming of the Shrew or The Tempest.
Analyse the play in close detail, including the effects of structure, form and language.
Consider issues raised in an extract in relation to the play as a whole.
Explore how the play has been interpreted by different audiences over time.
Give informed, personal and creative responses using literary terminology and accurate written expression.
Study one pre-1900 drama text: Edward II, The Duchess of Malfi, She Stoops to Conquer, A Doll's House or An Ideal Husband.
Study one pre-1900 poetry text: Chaucer's Merchant's Prologue and Tale, Paradise Lost Books 9 and 10, Coleridge, Tennyson's Maud or Rossetti selected poems.
Study one pre-1900 drama text: Doctor Faustus, The Duchess of Malfi, The Rover, A Doll's House or The Importance of Being Earnest.
Study one pre-1900 poetry text: Chaucer's Franklin's Prologue and Tale, Paradise Lost Books 1 and 2, or selected poems by Barrett Browning, Clare or Rossetti.
Explore contrasts, connections and comparisons between the chosen drama and poetry texts.
Explore how the texts relate to each other and to literary traditions, movements and genres.
Understand the significance of cultural and contextual influences on writers and readers.
Identify how attitudes and values are expressed in the texts.
Explore the texts informed by different interpretations.
Give informed, personal and creative responses using terminology and accurate expression.
Read widely and independently in the chosen topic area.
Analyse how writers shape meanings in unseen prose extracts.
Identify how attitudes and values are expressed in unseen extracts.
Communicate knowledge, understanding and judgement fluently, accurately and effectively.
Choose one topic from American Literature 1880-1940, The Gothic, Dystopia, Women in Literature or The Immigrant Experience, and study two whole texts, at least one a core text.
Study core texts The Great Gatsby and The Grapes of Wrath, or suggested texts such as Huckleberry Finn, The Age of Innocence, A Farewell to Arms and Native Son.
Study core texts The Bloody Chamber and Other Stories and Dracula, or suggested texts such as Frankenstein, The Picture of Dorian Gray, Rebecca and Beloved.
Study core texts The Handmaid's Tale and Nineteen Eighty-Four, or suggested texts such as Brave New World, Fahrenheit 451, A Clockwork Orange and The Road.
Study core texts Sense and Sensibility and Mrs Dalloway, or suggested texts such as Jane Eyre, Tess of the D'Urbervilles, The Bell Jar and Girl, Woman, Other.
Study core texts The Reluctant Fundamentalist and Call It Sleep, or suggested texts such as The Jungle, The Namesake, Brick Lane and Small Island.
Explore contrasts, connections and comparisons between texts within a topic area.
Explore how texts relate to one another and to literary traditions, movements and genres.
Explore how texts are interpreted by different readers over time.
Use literary critical concepts and terminology with understanding and discrimination.
Show understanding of the significance of contexts in which texts were written and received.
Study three post-1900 texts, one prose, one poetry and one drama, with at least one first published or performed in 2000 or later.
Show close reading skills and analyse how meanings are shaped in one chosen text.
Identify how attitudes and values are expressed in the chosen text.
Explore the contexts of two texts and others' interpretations of them.
Explore connections across two texts and how values are expressed in them.
Draw on different interpretations to evaluate the chosen texts.
